Choiaqo Published July 30th, 2026 - 07:26 GMT POZNAN, KRZESINY, POLAND - October 17, 2018: Polish Air Force F16 performs at the 31st Tactical Air Base. (Shutterstock) ALBAWABA - Polish police on Thursday found a crater and scattered debris in the Polish countryside near the border with Ukraine; the crater was left by an unidentified object that was tracked by army radars before it disappeared. Also Read Poland downs Russian drones in historic first for NATO "An unidentified object ​moving westward was detected in Polish airspace," the operational command ​of the Polish armed forces said on X, adding that after the sighting at 3:40 a.m it disappeared from radars. After the disappearance of the object, a Polish military helicopter was sent out to the last known location of the object where it found the crater. “A helicopter crew ‌located ⁠the probable crash site of the object in an undeveloped area near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia in the Lublin province. "Officers discovered ​a ⁠crater and scattered debris from an unidentified object in a field located about 2 km from the nearest buildings, between ⁠the ​villages," the police stated on X. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Al Bawaba English (@albawaba_english) The police added that said crater measured about 10 m wide and that there were multiple reports of a loud bang in Biłgoraj county between ​the villages of Tarnawa Kolonia and Biskupice. Poland has been wary of the close proximity of Russian attacks, especially the ones targeting the Ukrainian city of Lviv close to the Polish border, scrambling jets to intercept any potential threat to its airspace. Pre-emptive sirens sounded in Lublin for a few minutes warning residents of a potential attack but were halted when the cause was investigated. https://dailypost.ng/2026/08/06/bewene-p.text: Super Eagles defender, Abdullahi Bewene, has signed a new five-year contract with Czech club Baník Ostrava, DAILY POST reports. Bewene is now contracted to the Baniček until June 2031, putting an end to speculation over his future. The 21-year-old rose through the youth and B teams at Baník to the first team. The right-back has also earned recognition on the international scene with Nigeria. Bewene made his international debut for the Super Eagles in a friendly against Poland last month. The right-back also featured in the Super Eagles' 2-1 friendly defeat to Portugal. He also represented Nigeria at the U-17 level in the past.

Home Paid news feed Foto Agerpres Press Monitoring Bucharest Phone: +4 021.2076.110 President Dan says Romania improved its response to drone threat, but is not fully prepared Category: English Date: 2026-09-23 15:15:58 Foto: ALEX MICSIK / AGERPRES PHOTO Romania is still not fully prepared for the threat posed by drones, although it has improved its response capabilities, President Nicusor Dan said in an interview with journalist Jim Sciutto for CNN International's 'The Brief with Jim Sciutto' broadcast on Tuesday evening. When asked whether Romania's response to that threat was sufficient, President Dan explained that the drone phenomenon is new and Romania had the same problem as other states, however, he mentioned that improvements had been made and that the US supported Romania with equipment to detect and shoot down drones. Nicusor Dan also talked about Romania's diplomatic response following an incident in which two people were injured in a town in Romania, 10 kilometers from the border. He mentioned the closure of a Russian consulate near the Black Sea and said he believes the measure was a proportionate response. Asked what Russia is seeking to achieve by expanding its hybrid warfare, Nicusor Dan said that, in the case of drones, he does not consider them to be necessarily intentional, while, regarding disinformation, attacks on the critical infrastructure and acts of sabotage, he said Russia is seeking to undermine citizens' trust in the authorities and European countries' support towards Ukraine. Asked how likely Russia is to directly attack a NATO member state, Nicusor Dan said he did not consider such a scenario very probable in the next one or two years, but underscored that countries must be prepared, bringing to mind that in 2020 and 2021 few people would have expected Russia to attack Ukraine and attempt to conquer Kyiv. Moreover, Romania's president underscored that European leaders now understand the threat, are increasing the expenses for defence, cooperating more and recognising the need to rebalance Europe's and America's contributions to defence. Regarding the reduction in US troop numbers in Europe, Nicusor Dan brought to mind that Romania had around 1,500 US troops, 500 of whom were part of a rotational troop in Romania, Bulgaria and Hungary, and that those 500 troops had been withdrawn. Asked whether the withdrawal could encourage Russia to act more aggressively and whether Donald Trump is open to a larger US presence, the Romanian president said it would be a good signal to have proportional displacement of American troops inside Europe. He argued that the presence of US troops near the Black Sea, as well as in close to the Middle East and the Mediterranean area, is also a benefit for the United States. Asked to comment on doubts expressed by some German officials about Washington's willingness to defend Europe in the event of a Russian attack, the Romanian president said that, for a long time, the United States had contributed to Europe's defence, while Europe's contribution had not been proportional, including in economic terms. Nicusor Dan said Donald Trump was right to speak about the need to rebalance this contribution and noted that the US president had reaffirmed his commitment to Article 5 of NATO at the Ankara Summit. In respect to the support for Ukraine, Nicusor Dan said that Romania is contributing to the defence effort, aiding refugees and ensuring the transit of Ukrainian grain, as Ukraine can no longer use its ports. Asked what else Europe and NATO could do given the lack of air defence systems, he pointed to the issue of anti-ballistic interceptor production and said that countries had not been prepared for the scale of this need. Regarding the possibility of NATO shooting down Russian drones over Ukraine, following incidents in which such aircraft entered the airspace of member states, Nicusor Dan explained that, as he understood it, international rules could consider such an intervention an act of co-belligerence, mentioning that this is the answer he received when discussing the possibility of such an intervention with military representatives. In respect to a possible negotiation to end the war, the Romanian president said that, at the moment, he does not believe Moscow is willing to negotiate, adding that the support for Ukraine and sanctions against Russia must continue and argued that the Russian economy is suffering. At the same time, he quoted polls according to which the Russian society is increasingly expressing opposition to the war, saying that the share of those who no longer support the war had risen from 40% to 60%. He concluded by underscoring that Ukraine is an independent state that was attacked and must be supported. The CNN interview was conducted in New York, where Nicusor Dan is attending meetings of the UN General Assembly. https://www.dw.com/en/poland-krakow-shoo.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PILz Prefer DW on Google The suspect, now deceased, is suspected of radicalization and severe psychiatric issues Image: Jakub Porzycki/REUTERS Advertisement Polish Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek issued an update on Tuesday concerning the case of a mass shooting in Krakow over the weekend. Accused gunman Michal Oksinski was deeply interested in international far-right movements, Zurek said. "Authorities have accessed the terrorist's computer. It is clear that he visited websites concerning Anders Breivik ," the Norwegian neo-Nazi who killed 77 people in July 2011, the minister added. Zurek said a search of Oksinski's home turned up a Gadsen flag, a banner dating back to the US Civil War that is now associated with American white nationalists. Police also gathered evidence that he had recently bought 10 magazines for a semi-automatic rifle and 500 bullets. "It is clear that this individual was preparing to take action," the justice minister said. Krakow shooting suspect 'fascinated by far right' To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video What happened in the attack? On Friday night, 24-year-old Oksinski is thought to have shot and killed his mother, father, sister and two family cats in the city of Ostrowiec. The following day at around 3:00 p.m. local time, Oksinski is suspected of opening fire in Krakow's Main Market Square. Six people were killed — four Poles, one Austrian, and one UK national. Another 15 people were wounded. After the attack in Krakow, authorities discovered the bodies of his family members in Ostrowiec. Poland then observed two days of national mourning . Oksinski died of wounds sustained during his arrest at a local hospital on Monday. Initial investigations have uncovered "very solid" evidence pointing to far-right radicalization and psychiatric issues as motives for the attacks, Zurek said. However, Zurek and the centrist government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk has been accused by members of right-wing populist PiS party of lying about Oksinski's motives.
